analysis.title: Investors still shaken
key_insights: The CACIB FX Risk Index is at -0.6483 versus -0.8370 last week, continuing a gradual retreat from risk-seeking territory. It sits around its 100-day moving average, which the report says suggests the retreat could be prolonged.

Technology stocks remain under pressure despite Nvidia's earnings and forecast earnings surprising to the upside. New US restrictions on access to advanced chips, physical and remote, are worrying investors.

Data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil must obtain a US government license before allowing Chinese companies to remotely access advanced AI chips and servers. They also need a license to buy advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other US manufacturers. The report says it has not been specified whether US data centres face the same licensing.

Technology earnings are being discounted at a higher rate, which pressures the elevated valuations that depend on them. Strong US economic data and hawkish rhetoric from FOMC members have pushed UST yields back higher.
A Trump-Xi bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in Shenzhen on 19 November is flagged as important for the chip restrictions and investor sentiment.
The Anthropic IPO on 19 November is described as another big test for investor sentiment. The stock is reportedly six times oversubscribed. Crédit Agricole CIB is joint bookrunner on the IPO.

The Risk Index was driven higher over the past week by higher equity and FX volatility and by defensive stocks outperforming cyclical stocks. Lower gold prices and private-credit spreads capped the gains.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations.

sector_views.rationale: Tech stocks remain under pressure from US chip export restrictions and higher discount rates from rising UST yields, despite Nvidia's upside earnings surprise. The report does not state a formal sector rating.

earnings_insights: Nvidia's earnings and forecast earnings surprised to the upside per the report, which gives no EPS or revenue figures. Tech stocks stayed under pressure regardless.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from -0.8370 last week, a gradual retreat from risk-seeking territory. It is near the 100-day moving average, which suggests the retreat could be prolonged.
Strong US data and hawkish FOMC rhetoric pushed yields back higher, raising the discount rate on tech earnings.

risk_factors: US chip export licensing rules could widen to US data centres, which the report says is unspecified.
Higher UST yields discount tech earnings at a higher rate and pressure valuations.
The Trump-Xi meeting outcome on chip restrictions could move sentiment.
The Anthropic IPO could disappoint despite reported six-times oversubscription.
